description: Addition, subtraction and multiplication are exact within 34 digits (ADR-0002 §2.1). No case here carries a policy, because none of these operations is permitted to round.

provenance.oracle: General Decimal Arithmetic Specification — add, subtract, multiply
provenance.contentVersion: n/a — engine vectors, authored against the specification rather than against a content bundle

cases.oracle: Specification: the ideal exponent of add is min(exponent(x), exponent(y)), so two minor-unit amounts sum to a minor-unit amount. Scale is semantic — a line of 12.50 is not the same fiscal statement as one of 12.5.
Elementary arithmetic. In binary floating-point this is 0.30000000000000004; the case exists so that a regression to float64 fails here rather than in a tax return (Build Plan §8, High).
Elementary arithmetic. 0.30000000000000004 - 0.1 in binary floating-point is 0.20000000000000004.
Specification: multiply has exponent(x) + exponent(y), so 1234E-2 x 5E0 is 6170E-2. The trailing zero is carried, not trimmed.
Elementary arithmetic. A credit line multiplies like the debit line it reverses; the exponent is -2 + -1 = -3.
Specification: the result takes the finer of the two exponents, so a sub-minor-unit intermediate is not silently rounded to the coarser operand's scale (ADR-0002 §2.5).
34 significant digits is exactly the decimal128 coefficient width (ADR-0002 §2.1 and §4.4). The largest value the context represents exactly must survive an exact operation.

(1 + 1E-16)^2 = 1 + 2E-16 + 1E-32, which is 33 significant digits and therefore exact at precision 34. One digit more of input and the Inexact trap fires — see errors/mul-inexact-at-precision-boundary.
